The bilateral agreement remains in force for a period of **five (5) years** and is **renewed for a similar period** unless one party officially notifies the other, through diplomatic channels, of its desire to suspend or terminate the agreement. An OWWA membership stays active until the expiration of the OFW’s existing employment contract or after two (2) years from the contract effectivity, whichever comes first. This is stated in RA 10801 (Sec. 9) and reiterated in the OWWA Citizens Charter (2026, 1st Edition), page 19.

No.  Under Republic Act 11862, cases involving trafficking in persons **shall not be dismissed** based on an Affidavit of Desistance executed by the victim or their parents or legal guardians. Public and private prosecutors are directed to oppose and manifest objections to motions for dismissal, and any attempt to unduly pressure the complainant to execute such an affidavit is punishable. [RA_11862_relevant_excerpts.pdf, page 3]

The penalty for committing any act of trafficking in persons as defined in Section 4 (as amended by RA 10364) is:

- **Imprisonment of twenty (20) years**  
- **A fine of not less than One million pesos (P1,000,000.00) but not more than Two million pesos (P2,000,000.00)**  

This is stated in RA 10364, Sec. 12, which amends Sec. 10 of R.A. 9208. [RA_10364_relevant_excerpts.pdf, p2]

Under the **Migrant Workers Act (RA 8042)**, illegal recruitment carries **life imprisonment** when the offense is **classified as “economic sabotage”** as defined in the Act.  
The Act also states that the **maximum penalty** (the longest term of imprisonment and the highest fine) is imposed **when the person who was illegally recruited is under 18 years old** or when the illegal recruitment was **committed by a non‑licensee or a non‑holder of authority**.  

Sources:  
- RA 8042, Section 7(a) and (b) – life imprisonment for economic sabotage.  
- RA 8042, Section 7(b) and the “Provided, however” clause – maximum penalty for minors or non‑licensed offenders.
